name: Super Normal product
summary: The anonymous everyday object: a chair, a clock, a kettle or a shelf in matte white plastic, pale wood and steel, drawn so that it looks right and leaves no trace of the designer.

philosophy.core_thesis: A good object is one that nobody notices: it does its job, it fits the hand and the room, and it needs no explanation or signature.
design_principles: Draw the most usual form of the object; change a proportion by 5 to 10% and no more.
Use one matte colour on 90% of the surface: white, pale grey or the colour of the wood.
Round each edge with a radius of 2 to 6 mm so that the hand finds no sharp line.
Join the parts with a narrow gap of 1 to 2 mm; show no screw head on a main face.
Use one material for each part: pale wood for the frame, plastic for the shell, steel for the hardware.
Make the object for a long life: it uses standard parts and it ages without damage.
Print no logo and no ornament on the face of the object.
anti_patterns: Sculptural gestures that ask for attention
Visible brand marks on the face
Dark exotic woods and high gloss
A form that copies a historic style

form.geometry: The plain cylinder, the rounded rectangle and the shallow dome, with small softened edges.
form.silhouette: A familiar outline that fits a type: a chair has four legs and a seat, a kettle has a body and a handle.
form.edges: Soft edges with a radius of 2 to 6 mm; a thin shadow gap of 1 to 2 mm at each joint.
form.proportion: A chair seat is 45 cm high; a clock face is 20 to 30 cm wide; a kettle body is about 12 cm in diameter and 20 cm high.
form.ornament: None. The only mark is a small, quiet detail such as a hanging hole or a small dot of colour.
rules: Each object keeps the standard outline of its type, with a change of 10% or less.
Each object uses 1 or 2 materials in view.
Each edge has a radius of 2 mm or more.
Each joint has a gap of 1 to 2 mm or none.
A colour other than white, grey or the wood covers less than 5% of the object.

materials.rule: Matte plastic and pale wood make about 70% of the visible surface; steel, glass and plain cloth make the rest.

finish.gloss: 3–12 GU on plastic and wood; 20–40 GU on brushed steel
finish.patina: The style wants a surface that ages without marks: wood takes a soft tone, and plastic and steel stay as they are.

hardware.section: Rods and handles 8–14 mm; a tap body 25–35 mm
hardware.joints: Narrow gaps, hidden fixings on main faces, and a few screws on the back or the base.
hardware.handles: A thin bar, a small round hole or a flat tab cut into the body.
hardware.switches_and_taps: A flat rocker in matte white; a slim steel lever tap on a plain cylinder.

palette.strategy: White, pale grey and light wood, with one soft colour at most; no saturated accent.

manufacture.scale: Series of many thousand pieces from firms that make household goods, with parts that other models also use.
manufacture.signs: A small gate mark under the base, a thin shadow gap at each joint, and a part that fits across several models.

objects.form: flush rocker on a square plate
plain stacking chair with a plywood seat

positive: white wall clock with no numerals

evidence.title: Plywood chair, 1988: a precursor work, before the 2006 name
Thinking Man's Chair, 1986: a precursor work, before the 2006 name

emotion.target_response: Quiet ease: the viewer feels that the object is right, familiar and without effort.

use_cases: a calm flat or office moodboard
a clean still life for a catalogue
hardware schedules for a rental unit
avoid_when: The brief asks for a bold statement or a sculptural object.
The room needs ornament, colour or craft marks.

modifiers.how: Swap plastic for oak, stoneware and linen, and leave the marks of the hand.
Use a grid, a fine grey scale and visible controls.
Add laminate pattern, contrasting colour and stacked solids.

era_blend.note: A contemporary object in this style is the norm; a reissue of a 1980s piece is the faithful case.
